text.title: xUnit Testing Worked Examples
text.summary: A service unit test, a controller integration test with a substituted DbContext, and the Program shim they depend on — plus the two shapes the rules exist to prevent, and the test-plan manifest this methodology emits.

example.note: class-fixture-required. This is the first thing to check when a test project fails to build with "Entry point not found".

Dependencies arrive through the constructor, so xUnit's per-test instance is the whole lifecycle (constructor-injection). Both tests return `Task` (async-task-return). The id matcher is precise and the interaction is verified (precise-mock-matchers). The two invalid inputs are one `[Theory]`, so CI names the failing row (theory-for-params). Structural assertion via FluentAssertions (fluentassertions-not-assert).

antipattern.description: `public async void GetAsync_ExistingOrder_ReturnsDto()` with `_repo.Setup(r => r.GetAsync(It.IsAny<int>(), It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()))` and no `Verify`.
antipattern.reason: Two silent failures in one method: the runner cannot observe an exception on an `async void` signature, so the assertion failing looks like a pass; and the loose matcher means the test still passes when production calls the repository with the wrong id, or never calls it.

example.note: One host per class through `IClassFixture`, so the startup cost is paid once (class-fixture-required). The client comes from `factory.CreateClient()`, so the request goes through the real DI graph and middleware (webapplicationfactory-for-integration). The DbContext is substituted, so the production database is never reachable from a test. Use Testcontainers instead of SQLite wherever the assertion depends on real engine semantics (testcontainers-for-db).
